RAJYA SABHA
————
List of Questions for ORAL ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Friday, the March 7, 2003/Phalguna 16, 1924 (Saka)

(Ministries :  Agriculture; Chemicals and Fer tilizers; Environment and Forests;
Food Processing Industries; Human Resource Development; Ocean Development;
Railways; Science and Technology; Steel; Youth Affairs and Sports)
Total number of questions—20
Agreement for deep sea sand
mining
*241. SHRI N.K. PREMA-
CHANDRAN: Will the Minister of
ENVIRONMENT AND FORESTS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are aware that
the State Government of Kerala entered into
an agreement with a private firm for deep
sea sand mining;
(b) whether the Government of Kerala
sought the opinion of Central agencies on
the environmental impact before signing
agreement;
(c) whether Government subscribe to
the view that the dredging causes irreparable
damage to the Marine Eco System and
traditional fishing sector;
(d) whether Government propose to
conduct a study on the environmental impact
of sand mining through any Central
agencies; and
(e) the extent to which the Coastal Zone
Regulation  Act permits the mining of sea
sand?
Districts without education facilities
†*242. SHRIMATI PREMA
CARIAPPA:
SHRI MOTILAL VORA:
Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be pleased
to state:
(a) number of districts in the country as
on date where arrangements have not been
made to send the children for primary
education;
(b) whether Government have
formulated any special scheme to send the
poor children and those suffering from
poverty and starvation to school;
(c) if so, the details thereof; and
(d) if not, the reasons therefor?
Increase in college fees
*243. DR. C. NARAYANA REDDY:
Will the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether there is any proposal to
increase fees of college students of General
and Professional Courses;
(b) if so, by when it is likely to be
implemented; and

subsidies?
Starvation and mal-nutrition among
cattle
†*244. SHRIMATI SAROJ DUBEY:
SHRI MOOLCHAND
MEENA:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that cattle in our
country are victims of partial starvation and
extensive mal-nutrition;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor; and
(c) what steps are being taken by
Government for saving the cattle from
starvation and mal-nutrition?
Changes in history text books
*245. SHRI GHULAM NABI AZAD:
Will the Minister of HUMAN RESOURCE
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government propose to
make some changes in the history books;
and
(b) if so, the details thereof and the
reasons therefor?
Mid-day meal scheme
*246. SHRIMATI SHABANA
AZMI:
DR. PRABHA THAKUR:
Will the Minister of HUMAN
RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT be pleased
to state:
(a) whether the mid-day meal scheme
for primary schools has run into difficulties
because the Food Corporation of India has
threatened to stop supplies unless HRD
Ministry pays up its arrears amounting to
Rs. 500 crores;
(b) if so, whether the Ministry has not
so far paid the amount required by the FCI;
and
(c) if so, to what extent the FCI has
stopped supplies and steps Government
propose to take to resolve the issue?
Killing of snakes by Madaris
*247. SHRI R.K. ANAND:
SHRI SANTOSH
BAGRODIA:
Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT
AND FORESTS be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that snakes are
still caught all over the country and sacrificed
in Snake-Mongoose fights by Madaris (road
showman);
(b) if so, whether Government have
imposed a ban to save both the snakes and
mongoose;
(c) if so, the punishment against Madaris
indulging in such heinous act;
(d) if not, the reasons therefor; and
(e) whether Government feel the need to
register all Madaris in the country and to
restrict their collection of snakes at all times?
FPI proposals in Bihar
†*248. SHRI GAYA SINGH: Will the
Minister of FOOD PROCESSING
INDUSTRIES be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have any plan
to establish food processing industry in Bihar
keeping in view the production of potato in
Nalanda and Litchi in Vaishali; and
(b) if so, the details thereof?

Raising productivity of Agriculture in
dry areas
1697. MISS MABEL REBELLO:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have any plan
to raise productivity of agriculture in dry
areas of the country, if so, the details
thereof;
(b) whether Government would ensure
lending to small and medium farmers of
dry land who have less than five acres of
land; and
(c) the money allocated for farmers
having land holdings below five acres during
the last three years?
Drought/temperature adapted crops
1698. SHRI RAVULA CHANDRA
SEKAR REDDY: Will the Minister of
AGRICULTURE be pleased to state:
(a) what are the steps taken to make
our crops adapt to climatic change
especially in a drought like situation; and
(b) the contigency plan proposed to
ensure optimum yield even on change of
temperature pattern?
Crop strategy due to delayed
monsoon
1699. SHRI K. KALAVENKATA
RAO: Will the Minister of
AGRICULTURE be pleased to state:
(a) whether any alternate crop strategy
has been chalked out for badly affected
States due to delayed monsoon;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) the other proposed rational method
of supporting the income of farmers?
National Agriculture Insurance
Scheme
1700. S HRI C. RAMACHANDRA-
IAH: Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE
be pleased to state:
(a) the number of States that have opted
for National Agriculture Insurance Scheme
of the Central Government;
(b) what are the main features of the
scheme;
(c) the share of premium paid by the
Centre and the concerned States for the
scheme; and

Restriction on cattle movement
through U.P.
1701. SHRI LALU PRASAD: Will the
Minister of AGRICULTURE be pleased
to state:
(a) whether Government are aware
that the Uttar Pradesh Government has
placed restriction on movement of cattle
through its territory, either through road
or rail;
(b) whether this restriction has placed
many people engaged in cattle rearing and
dairy industries in Bihar to considerable
inconvenience; and
(c) if so, whether Government propose
to take steps to tackle this problem, if so,
by what time?
Milk production
†1702. SHRI KRIPAL PARMAR: Will
the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have
conducted any survey regarding
quantum of total production of milk, in
the Government and non-Government
sectors in the country State-wise;
(b) if so, the details thereof and quantum
of total requirement of milk daily, State-
wise; and
(c) what steps are being taken to meet
out the shortage of production of milk in
comparison to its consumption?
Hemendra Kumar Committee
†1703. SHRI RAM JETHMALANI:
SHRI LAJPAT RAI:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that a Committee
headed by Shri Hemendra Kumar was
constituted in August, 2002;
(b) if so, the terms of reference of the
Committee and whether it has submitted
its report to Government;
(c) if so, the suggestions made in the
report; and
(d) the number of suggestions
Government have decided to implement?
Licensing procedure for aquaculture
farms
1704. SHRI R. S. GAVAI: Will the
Minister of AGRICULTURE be pleased
to state:
(a) whether Government have received
requests from States to expedite licencing
procedure for aquaculture farms;
(b) if so, the reaction of Government
thereto;
(c) the reasons for delay in granting
licences;
(d) whether Government have assessed
the impact of non-issuing the licenses on

Banning import of poultry products
1705. SHRI K. RAMA MOHANA
RAO:
SHRI RAMA MUNI REDDY
SIRIGIREDDY:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are aware that
poultry products are imported from
various countries, including the countries
where diseases like Aian Influenza are
prevalent;
(b) if so, whether Government propose
to take any action to ban import of poultry
products from such countries;
(c) if so, the details thereof; and
(d) if not, the reasons therefor?

there is a sharp decline in output of
foodgrains during 2002-2003 as reported
in the Hindu' dated 12th February, 2003;
(b) if so, the factors responsible for
sharp decline in output of foodgrains;
